question: Do two CMP 170HX cards in one box beat one, and is TP=2 worth it without NVLink or P2P?

hardware.topology: PHB (both cards traverse the PCIe host bridge; no NVLink, no PCIe switch)

interconnect.gns_meaning: GPU not supported - P2P is fused off in the CMP SKU itself
interconnect.note: P2P is NOT blocked by IOMMU or ACS; it is unavailable on the mining SKU. No BIOS or kernel change recovers it.
interconnect.d2d_vs_h2d: Inter-GPU copies are host-staged, so device-to-device is no faster than host-to-device.
interconnect.vllm_warning: Custom allreduce is disabled because your platform lacks GPU P2P capability or P2P test failed.

software.note: Identical engine and flags to results/lab-2026-08-21.json, so TP=1 here is directly comparable to the single-card lab.

tp1.power_note: Box total across both cards; the idle second card contributes ~40 W.

two_tp1_servers.layout: Two independent vLLM servers, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 on port 8000 and =1 on port 8001, TP=1 each, no collectives between them.
two_tp1_servers.note: At 16 agents this beats TP=2 by 1.8x (754 vs 415). At 32 agents, which TP=2 cannot serve at max-num-seqs 16, it reaches 1253 tok/s - 3.0x the TP=2 16-agent figure on the same two cards.
two_tp1_servers.tradeoff: Each server is limited to a 64 GB card and a 1.19M-token KV pool, and you need a load balancer in front. There is no shared KV cache between the two.

deltas_tp2_vs_tp1.crossover: TP=2 wins below ~3 concurrent agents and loses above it.

findings: TP=2 raises single-stream decode 23% (57.5 -> 70.9 tok/s) because the weights are split and each card moves half as many bytes per token.
TP=2 collapses batch throughput: 608 -> 415 tok/s at 16 agents, a 32% loss. Per-agent falls 43.0 -> 30.4 tok/s. Reproduced three times within 0.3%.

The cause is P2P: nvidia-smi reports GNS (GPU not supported), so vLLM disables its custom allreduce and every layer's collective is host-staged at 5.85 GB/s. At batch 16 the allreduce payload grows with batch size, so the interconnect dominates.
Prefill is 75% slower under TP=2 (27.1 s -> 47.4 s on 48K tokens) - prefill is compute-and-collective heavy and suffers most from the slow link.
The real prize is the KV pool: 1.19M -> 2.98M tokens (9.11x -> 22.77x concurrency at 128K), because both cards' HBM holds cache.
Two cards at 16 agents (415 tok/s) are beaten by ONE card at 16 agents (608 tok/s) while drawing similar power.

Measured directly: two independent TP=1 servers deliver 754 tok/s at 16 agents and 1253 tok/s at 32 agents, versus 415 tok/s for TP=2. Sharding beats tensor-parallel by 1.8x to 3.0x on the same two cards.

recommendation.use_tp2_when: The model does not fit in 64 GB, or you need a KV pool deeper than one card can hold, or you are latency-bound on a single stream (+23% decode).
recommendation.use_two_tp1_servers_when: You are throughput-bound and the model fits in one card. Measured 3.0x better (1253 vs 415 tok/s). Costs a load balancer and gives up the shared KV pool.
recommendation.never_assume: Do not assume TP=2 scales throughput on a card without P2P/NVLink. Measure both.

caveats: One 27B dense checkpoint on one rental instance. MoE models and larger checkpoints will shift the crossover point.
No accuracy testing; these are throughput numbers only.
Power is nvidia-smi summed across both cards, not a lab-grade shunt. The idle-card baseline (~40 W) is included in TP=1 box totals.
